svg.title: Review a bounded deletion plan before applying it
svg.desc: Five steps read top to bottom for deleting expired debug sessions in one project. 1, a creator with retention.plan granted on the project or tenant (an environment grant does not count) requests a project-scoped plan; the server records at most 100 candidates, the plan expires in 15 minutes, and sessions must have expired before the 24-hour cutoff; nothing is deleted yet. 2, review the actual proposal: scope, creator, expiry, omissions, candidate revisions and references; the same creator decides whether to apply this exact plan ID. 3, inside the deletion transaction Weave rechecks scope, creator, current retention.apply authority, expiry, revision, cutoff and references, and blocks changed, missing or referenced candidates. 4, it deletes only eligible candidates and commits the manifest, accounting and audit together; a failed transaction rolls back. 5, retrying the same plan ID recovers the original manifest after a lost response. Workflow history, provider receipts, source fences, catalogs and outbox history are never deleted by this plan; archived runs are purged one at a time from execution management.
svg.text: Review a bounded deletion plan before applying it
The current deletion target is expired debug sessions in one project, not
general workflow history.
READ DOWN • Each arrow carries the result into the next step
1. Request a project-scoped plan
The creator needs retention.plan on the project or tenant.
The server records at most 100 candidates; the plan expires in
15 minutes. Sessions must be expired before the 24-hour
cutoff.
PLAN • Proposal and audit are retained; no sessions are deleted
2. Review the actual proposal
Inspect scope, creator, expiry, omissions, candidate
revisions, and references.
The same creator chooses whether to apply this exact plan ID.
REVIEW • Applying is a separate deliberate command
3. Recheck inside the deletion transaction
Check scope, creator, current retention.apply authority,
expiry, revision, cutoff, and references.
Changed, missing, or referenced candidates are blocked.
RECHECK • A plan is not permanent permission
4. Commit deletion and its accounting together
Delete only eligible candidates and commit manifest,
accounting, and audit.
A failed transaction rolls back its changes.
COMMIT • Retain the manifest as evidence
5. Recover a lost response with the same plan
Retry the same plan ID to recover the original manifest of an
already committed application.
RETRY • Do not invent a replacement deletion request
Omitted records keep their protection
Workflow history, provider receipts, source fences, catalogs, and outbox
history are never deleted here; archived runs are purged one at a time.

g.text: Review the exact plan; applying it rechecks every candidate.
